stem: In the political system of this period, a 'samanta' was a:
options: Subordinate chief or lord who owed allegiance to a greater king
solution: A samanta was a subordinate ruler/landlord who acknowledged the overlordship of a more powerful king and provided military support.

stem: The Rashtrakuta dynasty in the Deccan rose to power when Dantidurga overthrew his overlord belonging to which dynasty?
solution: In the mid-8th century, the Rashtrakuta chief Dantidurga overthrew his Chalukya overlord and performed the hiranya-garbha ritual.

stem: The Cholas rose to power in which region of India?
options: The Kaveri delta in the south
solution: The Cholas built their kingdom around the fertile Kaveri delta in the far south, with Thanjavur as a centre.

stem: The magnificent Rajarajeshvara (Brihadeshvara) temple at Thanjavur was built by which Chola ruler?
solution: Rajaraja I built the great Rajarajeshvara (Brihadeshvara) temple at Thanjavur in the early 11th century.

stem: The Chola ruler who led a naval expedition to Southeast Asia and a campaign up to the river Ganga was:
solution: Rajendra I sent naval expeditions against the Srivijaya kingdom (Southeast Asia) and marched to the Ganga, taking the title Gangaikonda.

options: A text in praise/eulogy of a ruler
solution: A prashasti is a Sanskrit eulogy composed to praise and glorify a ruler, often part of inscriptions.

stem: In Chola local administration, the assembly of brahmana landholders in a brahmadeya village was called the:
solution: The 'sabha' was an assembly of brahmana landowners in brahmadeya villages; the 'ur' was the assembly of non-brahmana landholders and 'nagaram' of merchants.

stem: The 'tripartite struggle' of this period was fought for control of which city?
solution: The Gurjara-Pratiharas, Rashtrakutas and Palas fought a long tripartite (three-way) struggle for control of Kannauj and the Ganga valley.

stem: The Pala dynasty ruled mainly over which region?
solution: The Palas ruled over eastern India (Bengal and Bihar) and were one party in the tripartite struggle.

stem: Cholas are especially renowned in art for their exquisite:
solution: Chola bronze images, made by the lost-wax technique — especially the dancing Shiva (Nataraja) — are among the finest in Indian art.
